Brand Sessions

A day in your working world.

The Work, Not A Backdrop

A brand session is a day in your working world. We photograph you doing the thing you actually do — in your shop, your studio, your kitchen, on the floor where the work happens — and come away with a library that covers your site, your about page, and a season of posts without repeating itself.

That is a different product from a headshot. A headshot answers one question: what do you look like. A brand library answers the harder one: what is it like to work with you. It is the difference between a page that looks like a template with your name on it and a page that could only be yours.

It also lasts. Most of my clients are still using frames from a session two and three years later, because the photographs are of the work rather than of a haircut and a season’s wardrobe.

Built To Your Brief

Nothing on the day is improvised. Within a week of booking you fill out a brand questionnaire — what your business actually does, who you’re talking to, and how you want to come across. Everything after that is built on your answers.

Then we get on a call and I bring back a direction: where we shoot, what we shoot, and the shot list we’ll work from. I send a mood board so we’re both picturing the same thing before the day arrives. Wardrobe, locations, and what you’re walking away with all get settled there, not on the morning.

On the day we work to a minute-by-minute timeline. That sounds rigid; it is the opposite. It means nobody is standing around deciding what happens next, and you get far more out of the hours you paid for. Clients are consistently surprised by how much ground a half day covers when the plan was made in advance.

Where These End Up

This is business money, so it should come back. Before we shoot I want to know where these are going: the site header, the about page, the deck you send investors, the profile photo on six platforms, the press kit, a season of posts, the booth graphic for the one trade show you do a year.

Knowing that changes what I shoot. Frames destined for a website header get shot wide with room for headline type. A library that has to carry a year of posting needs variety in wardrobe and setting that we plan for rather than hope for. A deck needs the unglamorous middle of the process, not just the hero shot.

Photographs don’t earn anything sitting in a folder. If your package includes it, we plan out where each frame goes together once the gallery lands — because the session isn’t finished when the shooting stops.

About me

It’s my goal to make photographs that tell your story.

My name is Mike Thezier (pronounced: tee-zee-ey) — my last name looks nothing like it sounds. I’m a film and digital photographer based in Southern California, shooting brand work for founders, makers and small teams.

I’ve photographed a brand designer’s studio, a novelist’s writing day, a label plant’s production floor, a marine emissions barge alongside a cargo ship, and a fintech team who wanted headshots that didn’t look like headshots. What those have in common isn’t a look — it’s that in each case the work itself was the interesting part, and my job was to notice it.

If you’re a gym, a coach or a health brand, that world has its own studio: Pilgrimage Media, built for it and run by me.

The experience

Before the shoot

Within a week of booking you fill out a brand questionnaire. It takes about twenty minutes and it is the most useful twenty minutes of the whole project — what your business does, who you’re talking to, how you want to come across, and what you have been embarrassed to use so far.

We get on a call and I bring back a direction: where we shoot, what we shoot, and the shot list. Then a mood board, so we are both picturing the same thing well before the day. Wardrobe, locations and deliverables are all settled here.

If you need permission for a location, a second set of hands, or a particular piece of the operation running while we shoot, this is when we find that out — not at eight in the morning on the day.

Shoot day

Two to eight hours, depending on your package and how many locations and outfits we’re covering. We work to a minute-by-minute timeline built from the shot list, so the day has a shape and nobody is improvising.

We cover headshots, working shots, lifestyle frames and environmental portraits — the core set a brand actually needs. If you have a team, we build their frames into the timeline rather than treating them as an afterthought at the end.

Most people tell me beforehand that they are bad in front of a camera. Almost nobody is actually bad at doing their own job while someone photographs it, which is what I am asking you to do. The frames people end up using most are usually the ones where they had forgotten to pose.

After the shoot

I cull and edit the whole set myself — one to four weeks depending on the size of the shoot and the time of year. You’ll know which end of that range you’re on before you book, and if you have a launch date, say so and we will work to it.

Everything arrives in a private online gallery: high-resolution files, yours to download and use. No watermarks, no per-image fees, no expiry on the gallery.

Then get them onto your site and your profiles while they are fresh. If your package includes the planning session, we sit down together and decide where each frame goes.

Usage & licensing

Every session includes twelve months of unlimited use on your own channels — your website, your social accounts, your email, your deck, your print collateral. That covers what almost every client needs, and there is nothing further to pay for it.

Two things are quoted separately, because they are worth materially more to the business using them: paid advertising, and use beyond twelve months or beyond your own channels — a distributor’s catalogue, a partner brand, out-of-home. If either is likely, tell me at the questionnaire stage and I will price it into the session rather than send you a surprise later.

This is standard for commercial photography and unfamiliar to anyone who has only booked portraits, so I would rather explain it here than have it come up awkwardly. The short version: use them everywhere you own, for a year, included.

Sessions & pricing

Essentials

2 hours · one location

$1,200

Built for a founder who needs a proper set of current images and does not yet need a year’s worth — a refresh, a launch, a new role.

  • A two hour session at one location
  • Headshots, working frames and environmental portraits
  • Questionnaire, vision call and shot list
  • 40–60 edited high-resolution images
  • 12 months unlimited use on your own channels

Half Day

4 hours · two setups

$1,950

Built for a business that needs a library rather than a portrait — enough variety to cover a site, an about page and a season of posts without the same frame appearing twice.

  • A four hour session across two locations or setups
  • Multiple wardrobe changes built into the timeline
  • Questionnaire, vision call, mood board and shot list
  • 80–120 edited high-resolution images
  • Team headshots for up to four people
  • 12 months unlimited use on your own channels

Why this over Essentials. Two hours gets you one look in one place. Four gets a second setting and a wardrobe change, which is the difference between images you rotate and images that run out. This is the tier most businesses actually need and the one I would book if it were my own company.

Full Day

8 hours · the whole operation

$3,200

Built for a team or an operation with more than one room worth photographing — the floor, the office, the product, the people, in one coordinated day.

  • A full eight hour day, multiple locations
  • The whole operation — people, process, product, space
  • Questionnaire, vision call, mood board and full shot list
  • 200+ edited high-resolution images
  • Team headshots for your whole team
  • A planning session after delivery, mapping frames to where they go
  • 12 months unlimited use on your own channels

Why this over a half day. A half day makes you look good. A full day documents the business — the process, the floor, the people who are not the founder. If you are hiring, raising, or selling something made rather than something said, this is the one that earns its cost back fastest.

Add-ons. Additional locations, a second shooter, drone work, and video are all available and quoted with the session rather than assumed. Headshot-only sessions and ongoing content libraries are priced separately — ask and I’ll send those.

Questions

Who owns the photographs?
I hold the copyright, as photographers do; you get a licence to use them. Every session here includes twelve months of unlimited use on your own channels, which is what almost everybody needs. Paid advertising and use beyond your own channels are quoted separately — see Usage & licensing above.
How many images do we actually get?
Between 40 and 200-plus depending on the tier, all edited and full resolution. Every frame delivered is one I would put in my own portfolio — you are not being handed a folder of near-duplicates to cull yourself.
We’re not photogenic and our office is ugly.
Both of those are my problem, not yours. Ugly offices photograph better than people expect once you know which corner to use and what time of day to use it, and that is part of what the vision call is for. If the space genuinely will not work, we will find somewhere that does before the day rather than discover it together.
Do you travel?
I’m based in the Temecula Valley and shoot across Southern California — Orange County, San Diego, Los Angeles and the Inland Empire are all regular trips at these rates. Further afield is possible; travel is quoted with the session.
How soon do we get them?
One to four weeks depending on the size of the shoot and the time of year. If you have a launch or a deadline, tell me when you enquire and I will tell you honestly whether I can make it.
What if we need more later?
Additional sessions are straightforward once the brief exists — the questionnaire and shot list carry over, so a follow-up takes less setup than the first one. Several clients shoot once a year to keep the library current.

Next step

Pick the session that fits and send it to me with your business, roughly when you’re hoping to shoot, and where the images are going. I’ll come back with dates and the questionnaire.

A 50% retainer holds your date and comes off the total; the balance is due on the day of the shoot. I’ll send the contract and the invoice through HoneyBook, so it’s signed and paid in one place. Until the retainer is in, the date stays open to whoever asks next.

Not sure which tier fits? Send me a message describing what you need the photographs to do and I’ll tell you which one I’d book — including if that is the smaller one.
